text: marie: FYI the docs linkcheck CI failed on a Docusaurus MDX page. It reports a missing fragment for `/guides/setup/#weird-legacy-heading` even though the H2 exists. jordan: I pulled the build logs. The generated HTML has the id `weird-legacy-heading-1` while the markdown link points to `#weird-legacy-heading`. Looks like slug dedupe kicked in because we have an auto-generated id and an explicit HTML anchor on the same page. tori: ah yeahI added an inline `` in that page to support a legacy embed. That probably collides with the remark-slug output. marie: mixing explicit anchors and generated ones is risky. We need a single source of truth: either authors add explicit anchors and we disable slugify for that header, or we normalize during build. jordan: quick reproduction: MDX file with header `## Weird legacy heading` plus inline HTML anchor yields two ids. Docusaurus/remark-slug will append `-1` to avoid duplicate ids. Linkcheck then fails if internal refs target the un-suffixed id. tori: what's the least disruptive fix? I can remove the inline span but there are a few pages still referencing the old anchor from external docs. marie: proposal: add a build-time normalizer that prefers explicit anchors when present, and emits HTML redirects (tiny fragment pages) so old `#weird-legacy-heading` links keep resolving to `#weird-legacy-heading-1`. Short-term patch to linkcheck to accept deduped suffixes would also unblock CI. jordan: alternatively, tweak the MDX preprocess to strip explicit inline anchors and convert them to explicit markdown anchors using `{#id}` syntax before remark-slug runs. That way IDs are consistent and dedupe won't happen. tori: converting inline HTML to markdown anchors sounds safe. I can run a codemod across /docs to change `` to an adjacent `{#x}` on the header. Could include in the same PR as the normalization. devops-bot: nightly/docs-linkcheck failed (https://ci.redwood.ai/build/9123) :x: | job: docs-linkcheck | duration: 7m marie: plan: 1) Jordan will prototype the MDX preprocess codemod that converts inline anchors to `{#id}` and adds a unit test. 2) Tori will run the codemod on affected pages and open a docs PR with the content cleanups and a short changelog in the PR description. 3) I'll open a small linkcheck tweak to accept `(-\d+)?` fragments to avoid transient CI failures. 4) Add a contributor note in contributing.md: avoid inline HTML anchors; use `{#anchor}` on the header or explicit HTML-only pages. jordan: I'll target the prototype branch tonight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1402 (draft). It includes tests and a script `tools/mdx-anchor-fix`. tori: thanks. I'll run the codemod and flag any pages that need manual attention (edge cases with raw HTML blocks). marie: great. Once those land, we'll rerun the nightly. If CI still flags external links, we'll generate tiny `/_redirects`-style fragment pages mapping old anchors to new ones as a last resort. :calendar: jordan: noted. tagging the PR `docs:hotfix` and will ping once ready for review. tori: ping me for the review; I can help validate localized copies too. marie: perfect thanks everyone :thumbsup:
